For every natural number n with n ≥ 2 and every real number r with 0 < r < 1, make the following local definitions. Let E = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), the real n-dimensional Euclidean space with its standard ℓ² norm and coordinates indexed by 0, …, n−1; let y₀ denote coordinate 0 of y ∈ E. Let j₀ ∈ Fin n be the index 0, which exists because n ≥ 2. Let S be the unit-sphere subtype Metric.sphere (0 : E) 1. Let λ be Euclidean Lebesgue measure on E and let τ = λ.toSphere be the measure on S: for a measurable subset A of S, τ(A) is n times λ of the cone {sζ : 0 < s < 1, ζ ∈ A}, where ζ is included in E. Let ι : S → E be subtype inclusion and define the measure σ on E by σ = (τ(univ))⁻¹ • (τ.map ι), where univ is the whole sphere subtype, τ.map ι is its ambient pushforward, and the inverse total mass and measure scalar multiplication use extended nonnegative real scalars. Define K : E → ℝ on all of E by K(y) = (1 + r² − 2r y₀)^(n/2), with n cast to ℝ in the exponent and this power interpreted as Real.rpow, which is defined for all real bases. Then both real-valued functions y ↦ 1/K(y) and y ↦ y₀/K(y) are genuinely Bochner integrable with respect to σ, and their real Bochner integrals over the entire ambient space E satisfy
∫_E 1/K(y) dσ(y) = 1/(1 − r²)
and
∫_E y₀/K(y) dσ(y) = r/(1 − r²).
All real divisions and inverses in these expressions use the totalized-at-zero convention. No additional positivity or support hypothesis is imposed.
